claim: Population SPK-SPK lead/lag correlation (area x functional_type nodes, +-100ms/10ms-step lag axis, trial-mismatch shuffle null, pool after testing) replaces Granger as the candidate SPK-SPK method per 2026-08-06 direction. Result: 4/12033 Holm, 35/12033 BH-FDR in the full (scope x node-pair x lag x condition-group) family. All Holm survivors and most BH survivors are at lag 0 or within +-30ms -- no corrected evidence of a substantial lead/lag delay; what survives is near-simultaneous coupling in a few specific area/functional-type pairs (V4 Null/S-, V4 S+/S-, FEF Null/S-), all within-area, small n_sessions (3-7).
method: smoke_test_sliding_trial_correlation.lagged_corr_same_trial (new function, shares _corr_and_null core with sliding_corr_same_trial -- refactor verified numerically identical on the existing LFP-LFP validated case before use); nodes = (area10, func_group) reused verbatim from extract_population_firing_lfp_power_corr.py; lag declared as a family axis (like window position in the LFP-LFP script), never a post-hoc max-over-lags selection -- confirmed 76-84% of pairs exceed |Z|>=1.96 at SOME lag by chance alone before correction, which is why this matters.
notes: Proportionally much weaker than fig07's LFP-power population result (19/480, ~4.0%) or fig05's GLMM (2/45, ~4.4%) -- here 0.033% Holm, driven by the 21-lag family size (12,033 cells vs 480/45), not necessarily a smaller true effect.

Granger SPK-SPK (0/27, fully null) stays as-is per direction; this is an alternative/candidate method, not yet decided whether it replaces Granger as fig06's headline or sits alongside it as a supplement -- explicitly flagged back to the user, not assumed.
17/21 sessions in the units table produced usable extraction output (4 skipped -- likely missing NWB files, same pattern as prior SPK-SPK/population scripts this week).

edges.note: different method, same corpus, both come back weak/null for SPK-SPK connectivity -- consistent finding across two independent methods, not a contradiction of substance
